cases.name: Selena Teresita Hidalgo Calderon
cases.about:
“My daughter and my grandson were my life, she was my first born and I feel like a piece of my heart is gone.”
-Estela Calderon, mother of Selena Hidalgo Calderon

"Selena Teresita Hidalgo Calderon was an 18-year-old mother, daughter, sister and farmworker, who often posed for pictures with a peace sign and referred to her close friends as mi amor (“my love”). She was born in Huehuetenango, Guatemala on Oct. 15, 1999 to Estela Calderon and Romulo Pablo Hidalgo Avila.

Selena, along with her mother and younger siblings, fled violence in their home country of Guatemala in search of asylum in the United States.

Despite the many hardships, Selena dreamed of becoming a teacher, maintained a joyful existence, and with her friendship brought laughter and respite to other migrant farmworkers.

“She was always happy and made us laugh,” said her friend María, who had worked with Selena on a dairy farm. María said they called each other often to maintain their friendship even after Selena moved to a remote area to work in an apple orchard.

It was in the Wayne County orchard where she was last employed that Selena was found dead on May 23, 2018. Selena had previously sought support as a survivor of domestic violence. Her 1-year-old son, Owen, is still missing.

The pain brought by the tragic circumstances of her death is immeasurable, but her vibrant and loving spirit endures as the gift that was her short life. It was with such loving spirit that she mothered her son and was a big sister to her siblings, Deivyn, Jaquelin, Clinton, and her 10-month-old sister, Crisbel, whom Selena named. Her mother describes her as deeply caring and patient with children and as someone who loved to look up recipes and cook.

Selena’s death is a loss to a family and a broader community. She has transitioned to a place we hope can meet the joy of her spirit. We urge all who read her story to remember her, as we do, and to reflect on the circumstances that made for her tragic death. We each can play a role to prevent this from happening to anyone else. If you suspect a woman is the victim of domestic violence, tell someone. Don’t leave her alone. If a woman seems to be suffering in silence, say something. But more importantly, if you can do anything to help end the cycle of government violence that relegates immigrant women and children to suffer in silence and in the shadows, do so. How Selena lived her short life teaches us all what it means to demand dignity and the right to happiness even when the conditions of life imposed by governments and heartless men want to rob us of our light."

cases.narrative:
"Wayne County District Attorney Michael Calarco would not comment in January on what evidence had been presented to the grand jury, including the cause of death or when the killings took place.

At a press conference Thursday at the Wayne County Sheriff's Office in Lyons, Calarco said Donoteo-Reyes "had to admit and acknowledge that he caused their deaths." But law enforcement officials didn't release a cause of death."

https://www.democratandchronicle.com/story/news/2019/09/11/everardo-donoteo-reyes-alberto-reyes-sodus-ny-selena-hidalgo-calderon/2291782001/

Her body was found buried at Sodus Farm. Photos taken from trail cams showed Donoteo-Reyes walking in and out of the wooded area. In one photo, he was carrying a shovel.
